skill.name: siteground-cache
skill.description: Bypass SiteGround, LiteSpeed, and browser caching for WordPress staging development by adding a removable cache-busting snippet to a child theme.
skill.summary: Adds and removes a staging-only WordPress cache-busting helper for SiteGround development workflows.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown-related static findings are false positives caused by code fences and inline examples. The bundled shell scripts are scoped local file editors, but the skill contains substantive risks in credential handling and insecure FTP deployment guidance. Publication should require clearer secret-handling safeguards and secure transfer instructions.

remediation.issue: Plaintext credential collection and storage guidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions to store FTP passwords in CLAUDE.local.md. Use temporary interactive prompts, a password manager, or short-lived deployment credentials that are not persisted in project files.
Replace ftp:// examples and disabled certificate verification with SFTP or FTPS. Keep certificate verification enabled and avoid putting passwords directly in command examples.

remediation.issue: Shell scripts modify WordPress theme files
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run mode, explicit confirmation, stronger path validation, and restore instructions before installing or removing code from functions.php.

content.user_title: Bypass SiteGround Cache for WordPress Staging
content.value_statement: WordPress developers often cannot see theme changes because SiteGround, LiteSpeed, or browser caches serve old assets. This skill adds and removes a staging-only cache-busting snippet for child themes and guides verification.
actual_capabilities: Adds a predefined PHP cache-busting snippet to a child theme functions.php file.
Creates timestamped backups before installing or removing the snippet.
Removes the cache-busting functions and related comment blocks from functions.php.
Shows an admin-only development banner with the active theme name and version.
Adds no-cache headers and timestamp query strings for theme CSS and JavaScript.
Documents a staging-first workflow for SiteGround and LiteSpeed cache testing.
limitations: It is intended for staging or local development, not production automation.
It requires direct access to a WordPress child theme directory.
It does not manage SiteGround control-panel cache settings or CDN purges.
The deployment guidance handles credentials, so users must protect secrets separately.

use_cases.title: Preview Theme Changes on Staging
use_cases.description: Add temporary cache bypass logic so CSS and JavaScript changes appear during SiteGround staging review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Clean Production Release
use_cases.description: Remove the development cache buster and verify that temporary functions are gone before launch.

use_cases.title: Debug SiteGround Cache Behavior
use_cases.description: Check whether LiteSpeed, SG CachePress, browser cache, or CDN layers are hiding recent theme changes.

prompt_templates.title: Install on Staging
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a known child theme path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add SiteGround cache busting to the staging child theme at [path]. Create a backup first and summarize what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Cache Bypass
prompt_templates.scenario: Confirm that the development banner and asset timestamps are working.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether the SiteGround cache buster is active on staging. Review the theme files and list safe verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Remove Before Launch
prompt_templates.scenario: Clean up temporary development code before production release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Remove the SiteGround cache buster from the child theme at [path]. Preserve a backup and confirm which functions were removed.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Secure Deployment
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of transfer method and credential handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staging deployment plan for this SiteGround cache-busting change. Flag credential risks, insecure transfer steps, and production safety checks.

output_examples.input: Add cache busting to my staging child theme.
output: Confirms the target is a staging child theme.
Creates a backup of the current functions.php file.
Adds the cache-busting functions and reports the inserted behavior.
Provides staging verification steps for the admin banner and refreshed assets.

output_examples.input: Remove the cache buster before production release.
output: Creates a fresh backup before cleanup.
Removes the SiteGround cache-busting functions and related comments.
Summarizes what was removed and recommends a final staging check.

output_examples.input: Review my SiteGround staging deployment plan.
output: Identifies whether the plan uses staging-only paths.
Calls out credential storage and plain FTP risks.
Recommends safer transfer and rollback steps.

best_practices: Use this only on staging or local development and remove it before production release.
Keep backups of functions.php and review inserted PHP before deployment.
Prefer SFTP or managed deployment over plain FTP when transferring files.
anti_patterns: Do not store real FTP passwords in shared project files or commit them.
Do not use the cache buster as a permanent production performance setting.
Do not deploy to production only because a path or host name contains staging.

faq.question: Does this skill disable caching for all visitors?
faq.answer: No. The included PHP checks for administrator capability before adding headers, banners, and asset timestamps.

faq.question: Can I use it on production?
faq.answer: It is designed for staging and development. Remove the snippet before production release.

faq.question: Does it purge SiteGround or Cloudflare caches?
faq.answer: No. It changes WordPress output for administrators and adds asset timestamps, but it does not call hosting or CDN APIs.

faq.question: What files does it modify?
faq.answer: The installer and remover target the child theme functions.php file and create timestamped backups.

faq.question: Is FTP required?
faq.answer: No. The documentation includes FTP examples, but SFTP or a managed deployment workflow is safer.

faq.question: What should I check after installing it?
faq.answer: Log in as an administrator on staging, confirm the banner appears, and verify CSS or JavaScript URLs include fresh version parameters.
